title: Point Loma 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: Point Loma 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Point Loma 1031 Exchange Coordination in San Diego, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Point Loma naval-adjacent and marina-district owners in San Diego, covering Liberty Station repositioning and QI handoffs.

sections.html: Point Loma is a peninsula neighborhood defined by two active naval installations, a converted former naval training center now known as Liberty Station, and marina-facing commercial space along Shelter Island and Harbor Island. An owner exchanging out of Point Loma property is working in one of the more specialized corners of the San Diego market, and coordination should reflect that specialization rather than treat it like a standard coastal deal.

sections.heading: What Actually Trades on This Peninsula
sections.html:
Liberty Station, the redeveloped former naval training center, carries a mix of retail, office, and cultural-use space under a master lease and ground-lease structure that differs from fee-simple ownership found elsewhere in San Diego. Shelter Island and Harbor Island hold marina-facing hospitality, restaurant, and marine-services commercial parcels, many tied to boat slip access and coastal permitting history.

Residential and small multifamily along Point Loma's upper bluffs and near Sunset Cliffs trade at some of the highest per-unit values in San Diego County, reflecting both view premiums and limited buildable land. A smaller stock of older bayside cottages and duplexes near the base gates trades at a steadier, lower price point, drawing a different buyer than the bluff-top view properties.

sections.heading: What Drives Demand Here
sections.html:
Naval Base Point Loma and Naval Base San Diego together anchor steady employment-driven housing demand that holds up independent of the broader San Diego tourism cycle. Marina and boating activity along Shelter Island and Harbor Island drives commercial demand tied specifically to marine services, boat sales, and waterfront dining rather than general retail trends.

Land scarcity on the peninsula, bounded by water on three sides, is the third driver, keeping replacement buyers focused on renovation and repositioning rather than new construction. Liberty Station's continued lease-up of retail and office space adds a fourth, more recent driver, as the redevelopment has matured into a steady draw for both shoppers and tenants from across San Diego.

sections.heading: Watchouts on a Point Loma Replacement Property
sections.html:
A few conditions are specific enough to this peninsula to check before identification.

  • Ground-lease versus fee-simple ownership structure on any Liberty Station parcel, which changes financing and exit options significantly
  • Coastal Commission review timelines on marina-facing parcels near Shelter Island and Harbor Island
  • Boat slip or marina lease terms tied to a commercial parcel, which may not transfer automatically to a new owner
  • Naval base proximity restrictions affecting certain uses or construction near the installations
  • View-easement or height-restriction covenants on bluff-top residential and small multifamily parcels

sections.heading: What a Standard Coastal Exchange Quote Overlooks
sections.html:
A coordination proposal written for a generic coastal San Diego deal usually assumes fee-simple ownership, which does not hold for a Liberty Station parcel operating under a ground lease, a structure that changes both financing terms and how proceeds and boot are calculated at closing. It also tends to skip whether a marina-facing property's boat slip agreements transfer with the sale, an issue that can materially affect value if left unresolved.

Before signing an engagement letter, confirm the proposed coordinator has actually reviewed the specific lease or ownership structure on the relinquished property, beyond simply knowing its location within San Diego. A coordinator who treats a ground lease and fee-simple parcel identically is missing a distinction that changes the entire financing conversation.

faqs.q: Does a ground-lease structure at Liberty Station affect 1031 exchange eligibility?
faqs.a: A leasehold interest of 30 years or more, including renewal options, can qualify as like-kind real property, but the specific lease terms should be reviewed with a tax advisor before assuming eligibility, since shorter or more restrictive ground leases may not meet the threshold. This distinction should be settled well before an identification letter goes out on a Liberty Station candidate, since it can change which lenders are even willing to quote the deal.

faqs.q: Can boat slip agreements transfer automatically when a marina-facing property is identified as a replacement?
faqs.a: Not necessarily; slip agreements are often separate contracts tied to the marina operator rather than the real estate itself, so an investor should confirm transferability directly with the marina before relying on slip access as part of the property's value. That confirmation should happen before the property is identified, not after the exchange has closed and the slip access turns out to be missing.

faqs.q: How do naval base proximity restrictions affect a replacement property near Point Loma?
faqs.a: Certain construction heights or uses can be restricted near active naval installations, so any redevelopment plans for a candidate replacement property should be checked against those restrictions before the property is formally identified within the 45-day window. Overlooking those restrictions can quietly limit the value of a planned addition or redevelopment.

faqs.q: Who confirms the boot calculation on a ground-lease-to-fee-simple exchange?
faqs.a: The investor's tax advisor or CPA should confirm boot exposure, since exchanging between a leasehold interest and fee-simple ownership can raise valuation questions that need careful review before the exchange closes. This distinction matters most for Liberty Station parcels, where the ground-lease structure is the norm rather than the exception.

faqs.q: Should I confirm coastal permitting history before identifying a Shelter Island or Harbor Island parcel?
faqs.a: Yes, prior coastal permitting decisions on a candidate property can affect what future improvements are allowed, and that history should be reviewed alongside the investor's own advisor before committing to identification. Waterfront parcels here often carry permitting conditions that are not obvious from a standard title report.
